  examples: "\n▶ {Hegh bey:sen:nolink}\n   {HeghDI' tlhIngan SuvwI' pagh tlhIngan\
    \ SuvwI' HoHlu'DI' Heghtay lulop latlh tlhInganpu'. Heghtay luloptaHvIS chaH chaq\
    \ bey SeQ lujach. Heghpu'bogh tlhIngan mInDu' lupoSmoHlu'. beyHom bey bey'a' jachtaH\
    \ latlh tlhInganpu'. yay 'oS bey. 'IQ pagh. Heghpu'bogh latlhpu' ghuHmoH bey.\
    \ ghoS tlhIngan SuvwI' maq.:sen:nolink}\n  \"Death Howl\n   When a Klingon warrior\
    \ dies or is killed, other Klingons may perform a ceremonial howl or yell as part\
    \ of the Klingon death ritual. The eyes of the fallen Klingon are opened and others\
    \ roar in a great crescendo. This yell is victorious in nature, rather than mournful\
    \ and also serves to warn the other dead that a Klingon warrior is coming.\"[1]"
  sources:
    raw: '[1] {SkyBox S31:src} (reprinted in {HQ 6.2, p.9, Jun. 1997:src})'
    citations:
    - source: skybox_s31
      reprinted_in:
        source: holqed
        page_start: 9
        volume: 6
        issue: 2
        date: Jun. 1997
  translations:
    de:
      definition: Todesschrei
    fa:
      definition: ضرب و شتم مرگ
    sv:
      definition: döden skriker
    ru:
      definition: Смертельный вой
      examples: "\n▶ {Hegh bey:sen:nolink}\n   {HeghDI' tlhIngan SuvwI' pagh tlhIngan\
        \ SuvwI' HoHlu'DI' Heghtay lulop latlh tlhInganpu'. Heghtay luloptaHvIS chaH\
        \ chaq bey SeQ lujach.Heghpu'bogh tlhIngan mInDu' lupoSmoHlu'. beyHom bey\
        \ bey'a' jachtaH latlh tlhInganpu'. yay 'oS bey. 'IQ pagh. Heghpu'bogh latlhpu'\
        \ ghuHmoH bey.ghey. ghoS tlhIngan SuvwI' maq.:sen:nolink}\n  \"Смертельный\
        \ вой.\n   Когда клингонский воин умирает или его убивают, другие клингоны\
        \ могут исполнять церемониальный вой или крик, как часть клингонского смертельного\
        \ ритуала. Глаза павшего клингона открыты, и остальные рычат в нарастающем\
        \ объеме. По природе этот вой скорее победоносный, нежели печальный. Также\

  notes: 'If {Hoch:n:nolink} is followed by a noun which is explicitly plural, it
    means "all the X''s", taken collectively. If the following noun is not explicitly
    plural, then it means "each X", considered individually.[2]


    If {Hoch:n:nolink} follows a noun, it means "all of X".[4] Note that this is different
    from {naQ:v} following a noun, which means "a complete X".'
  hidden_notes: This was defined as "everyone, all, everything" in {TKD:src}. The
    meaning "each" was added based on an article in {HolQeD:src}.[2]
  examples: "\n▶ {Hoch tlhInganpu':sen:nolink} \"all Klingons\"[2]\n▶ {Hoch paqmey:sen:nolink}\
    \ \"all the books\"[2]\n▶ {Hoch 'ebmey tIjon.:sen} \"Capture all opportunities\"\
    \ (and not \"each opportunity\")\n▶ {wo' toy'taHvIS Hegh 'e' tul Hoch tlhIngan.:sen}\
    \ \"To die while serving the Empire is the hope of every Klingon\" (i.e., every\
    \ Klingon, individually)\n▶ {targhlIj yab tIn law' no'lI' Hoch yabDu' tIn puS!:sen}\n\
    ▶ {nIn Hoch natlhlu'pu'.:sen}\n▶ {chalqachlIj rachlu'ta'bogh tutDaq:sen:nolink}\n\
    \   {mol'egh betleH:sen:nolink}\n   {muptaHvIS tay''eghmoH QeHDaj Hoch:sen:nolink}\n\
    \  \"The bat'leth sunk into the post\n   Of your fortified tower,\n   All his\
    \ rage focussed in one blow\"[3, p.158-159]\n▶ {qeylISvaD jach 'ej beyDaj luqImmo':sen:nolink}\n\
    \   {yuQDaq ghaHtaHbogh Hoch tlhIngan'e':sen:nolink}\n   {Qomqa' Hoch Qo'noS nuvpu':sen:nolink}\n\
    \  \"All of Kronos trembled once more,\n   For every Klingon on the planet\n \
    \  Followed her cry for Kahless.\"[3, p.186-187]"
  sources:
    raw: '[1] {TKD:src}, [2] {HQ 5.2, p.11, Jun. 1996:src}, [3] {paq''batlh 2ed:src},
      [4] {KLI mailing list 2022.05.27:src}'
    citations:

      page_start: 11
      volume: 5
      issue: 2
      date: Jun. 1996

      date: '2022-05-27'

  notes: 'The Klingon week has six days, which are:

    ▶ {DaSjaj:n} "Monday"

    ▶ {povjaj:n} "Tuesday"

    ▶ {ghItlhjaj:n} "Wednesday"

    ▶ {loghjaj:n} "Thursday"

    beginning with {wa'':n:num}. Thus, "Sunday" would be {jaj wa'':n}. The eighth
    day of the week on {lenmaq:n}, which uses an eight-day week, is called {jaj cha'':n:nolink},
    and so on.[2]'

      notes: 'Клингонская неделя имеет 6 дней, которыми являются:

        ▶ {DaSjaj:n} "Понедельник"

        ▶ {povjaj:n} "Вторник"

        ▶ {ghItlhjaj:n} "Среда"

        ▶ {loghjaj:n} "Четверг"

        ▶ {buqjaj:n} "Пятница"

        ▶ {lojmItjaj:n} or {ghInjaj:n} "Суббота"


        Если инопланетный календарь состоит более чем из 6 дней, дополнительные дни

    is actually a shortened form of {tlhIngan wo'' Hol:n:nolink}.[2]'

  part_of_speech: n
  pos: n
  status: canonical
  section: main
  definition: stringed instrument (general term)
  notes: 'This is the general term for a musical instrument with strings ({SIrgh:n}),
    which one may either pluck ({pang:v}) or strum ({yach:v:2}). To vary the sound,
    one "fingers" ({Heng:v}) the strings (touch them at different points while plucking
    or strumming).[1]


    Types of {HurDagh:n:nolink} include the {Supghew:n} (small), the {leSpal:n} (medium),
    and the {tIngDagh:n} (large).


    A {HurDagh:n:nolink} is not generally played with a bow, but a {ngItHel:n} may
    be plucked, strummed, or bowed.'

  notes: 'The Klingon day goes from dawn to dawn. For the part of a day during which
    there is daylight, see {pem:n} (the opposite of which is night, {ram:n}).


    The parts of a {jaj:n:nolink} are: {pem:n} "daytime", {jajlo'':n} "dawn", {po:n:1h}
    "morning", {pemjep:n} "midday", {DungluQ:n} "noon", {pov:n} "afternoon", {ram:n}
    "night", {ramjep:n:1} "midnight".


    For "days ago" and "days from now", see {Hu'':n} and {leS:n}, respectively.'

    raw: '[1] {TKD:src}'
    citations:
    - source: tkd
  translations:
    de:
      definition: Tag (von Sonnenaufgang bis Sonnenaufgang)
      notes: 'Der klingonische Tag geht von Sonnenaufgang bis Sonnenaufgang. Für die
        Teile eines Tages währendderen es hell ist, siehe {pem:n} (dessen Gegenteil
        ist Nacht, {ram:n}).


        Die Teile eines Tags {jaj:n:nolink} sind: {pem:n} "Tag, tagsüber", {jajlo'':n}
        "Morgendämmerung", {po:n:1h} "Morgen, Vormittag", {pemjep:n} "Mittag", {DungluQ:n}
        "Mittag", {pov:n} "Nachmittag", {ram:n} "Nahct", {ramjep:n:1} "Mitternacht".


        Für "vor x Tagen" und "in x tagen", siehe {Hu'':n} und {leS:n}.'

      definition: روز (از سپیده‌دم تا سپیده‌دم)
    sv:
      definition: dag, dygn (från gryning till gryning)
    ru:
      definition: День (от рассвета до рассвета)
      notes: 'Клингонский день продолжается от рассвета до рассвета. Для светового
        дня, смотрите {pem:n} (противоположность которому ночь, {ram:n}).


        Части {jaj:n:nolink}: {pem:n} "время дня", {jajlo'':n} "рассвет", {po:n:1h}
        "утро", {pemjep:n} "полдень", {DungluQ:n} "полдень(12:00p.m)", {pov:n} "после
        полудня", {ram:n} "ночь", {ramjep:n:1} "полночь".

  notes: This is really a shortened form of {javtIm ngeb raS'IS:n@@javtIm:n, ngeb:v,
    raS'IS:n}. Use of the term {raS'IS:n} is a holdover from ancient forms of medicine.

    or receiving a vaccine. For administering a vaccine, one might still hear the
    verb {poch:v}, as in {javtIm raS'IS poch Qel:sen@@javtIm raS'IS:n, poch:v, Qel:n:1h}.
    One could also say {javtIm raS'IS pochmeH Hergh QaywI' lo' Qel:sen@@javtIm raS'IS:n,
    poch:v, -meH:v, Hergh QaywI':n, lo':v, Qel:n:1h}. But it's more common to say
    simply {javtIm raS'IS Qay Qel:sen@@javtIm raS'IS:n, Qay:v, Qel:n:1h}, as in a
    medical context the verb {Qay:v} normally implies a {Hergh QaywI':n} was used.[1]
  components: '{javtIm:n}, {raS''IS:n}'
  sources:
    raw: '[1] {KLI mailing list 2021.02.28:src}'
    citations:
    - source: kli_mailing_list
      date: '2021-02-28'
  translations:

      definition: Impfstoff
      notes: Dies ist eine abgekürzte Form von {javtIm ngeb raS'IS:n@@javtIm:n, ngeb:v,
        raS'IS:n}. Die Benutzung des Worts {raS'IS:n} ist von antiken Formen der Medizin
        übriggeblieben. Dieses Nomen ist üblicherweise das Objekt des Verbs {SIQ:v},
        wenn man eine Impfung erhält. Für das Ausführen einer Impfung, kann man noch
        das Verb {poch:v} zu hören bekommen, wie in {javtIm raS'IS poch Qel:sen@@javtIm
        raS'IS:n, poch:v, Qel:n:1h}. Man könnte auch {javtIm raS'IS pochmeH Hergh
        QaywI' lo' Qel:sen@@javtIm raS'IS:n, poch:v, -meH:v, Hergh QaywI':n, lo':v,
        Qel:n:1h} sagen. Aber es ist üblicher einfach {javtIm raS'IS Qay Qel:sen@@javtIm
        raS'IS:n, Qay:v, Qel:n:1h} zu sagen, da in einem medizinischen Kontext das
        Verb {Qay:v} normalerweise impliziert, dass eine {Hergh QaywI':n} benutzt

      notes: Il s'agit d'une forme abbrévié de {javtIm ngeb raS'IS:n@@javtIm:n, ngeb:v,

        Qel:n:1h}. On pourrait aussi dire {javtIm raS'IS pochmeH Hergh QaywI' lo'

entry:
  entry_name: jav mIS
  slug: jav_mIS_n
  part_of_speech: n:deriv,slang
  pos: n
  categories:
  - slang
  metadata_tags:
  - deriv
  status: canonical
  section: main
  definition:
    text: confused prisoner, mixed-up prisoner, mixed-up six
    parts:
    - text: confused prisoner
    - text: mixed-up prisoner
    - text: mixed-up six
  notes: This is a slang expression used to refer to somebody who's in a bind, i.e.,
    in a situation they're not quite sure how to get out of. Some Klingons have started
    using {jva:sen:nolink} (in {pIqaD:n}) as a way to write {jav mIS:n:nolink} (though,
    when spoken out loud, this would still be pronounced as {jav mIS:n:nolink}).[1]
  hidden_notes: The creation of {jva:sen:nolink} was prompted by a typo (in {pIqaD:n:nolink})
    made on playing dice produced for the {Saarbrücken qepHom'a' 2022:src}.[2]
  search_tags: jva
  sources:
    raw: '[1] {Saarbrücken qepHom''a'' 2022:src}, [2] {KLI mailing list 2022.11.23:src}'
    citations:
    - source: qephom_2022
      date: '2022'
    - source: kli_mailing_list
      date: '2022-11-23'
  translations:
    de:
      definition: verwirrter Gefangener
      notes: Dies ist ein Slangausdruck, der sich auf jemanden bezieht, der in der
        Klemme sitzt, d.h. in einer Situation, von der er/sie nicht weiß, wie er/sie
        ihr entkommen soll. manche Klingonen haben begonnen {jva:sen:nolink} (in {pIqaD:n})
        zu benutzen, als eine Art {jav mIS:n:nolink} zu schreiben (wobei man dies
        laut immer noch {jav mIS:n:nolink} aussprechen würde).[1]
    fa:
      definition: زندانی گیج، زندانی مختلط، شش
    sv:
      definition: förvirrad fånge, blandad fånge, blandad sex
    ru:
      definition: сбитый с толку заключенный, растерянный узник, запутавшаяся шестёрка
    zh_HK:
      definition: 困惑的囚犯、混亂的囚犯、混亂的六人
    pt:
      definition: prisioneiro confuso
    fi:
      definition: henkilö tiukassa paikassa tai vaikean valinnan edessä
    fr:
      definition: prisonnier confus, prisonnier désorienté, six confus
      notes: Ceci est une expression familière qui s'utilise pour quelque'un qui est
        dans le pétrin, c.a.d., dans une situation difficile dont il/elle ne sait
        pas comment l'échapper. Quelques klingons ont commencé à utiliser {jva:sen:nolink}
        (en {pIqaD:n}) comme une maniére d'écrire {jav mIS:n:nolink} (cependant, il
        se prononce toujours {jav mIS:n:nolink} en parlant).[1]

entry:
  entry_name: jIb
  slug: jIb_n
  part_of_speech: n:body
  pos: n
  pos_subtype: body
  status: canonical
  section: main
  definition: hair (on head)
  see_also: '{chIp:v}, {SIrgh:n}, {veD:n}, {qur''ep:n}, {wan:v}, {tIy:v}'
  notes: 'This refers only to hair on the top of the head, and not to facial hair
    (see {rol:n} and {loch:n}) or body hair (see {pob:n}).[2]


    Animals do not have {jIb:n:nolink}, but {pob:n:nolink}.[3]


    To talk about someone being bald, simply say {jIb Hutlh:sen@@jIb:n, Hutlh:v}.[4]


    Long hair can be {jIb tIq:n@@jIb:n, tIq:v}, which is also the most common way
    to refer to a single long hair or several strands or a lock of long hair no longer
    on someone''s head. A common way to refer to a coiffure of long hair is to say
    {Qa jIb:sen@@Qa:v, jIb:n} (even if talking about a wig).[6]


    Short can be {jIb run:n@@jIb:n, run:v}, though another, perhaps more common, locution
    is to say the hair has been cut or trimmed (using {chIp:v} as in {jIb chIplu''bogh:n@@jIb:n,
    chIp:v, -lu'':v, -bogh:v} and so on). A single short strand of hair or a lock
    of shorter hairs no longer on a head would be {jIb wIl:n@@jIb:n, wIl:v} rather
    than {jIb run:n@@jIb:n, run:v}.[6]'
  hidden_notes: 'The "cut of someone''s jib" is an idiom referring to their appearance.


    Based on the examples, this is a mass noun.'
  examples: "\n▶ {DaH jIbwIj vISay'nISmoH.:sen}\n▶ {jIbDaj lumeQmoH:sen:nolink}\n\
    \   {jIbDaj lumeQmoH:sen:nolink}\n   {qul bIQtIq qulHommey:sen:nolink}\n  \"Sparks\
    \ from the fire river\n   Caught his hair,\n   Caught his hair.\"[5]"
  search_tags: bald
  sources:
    raw: '[1] {TKD:src}, [2] {qep''a'' 24 (2017):src}, [3] {KLI mailing list 2021.11.11:src},
      [4] {Saarbrücken qepHom''a'' 2021:src}, [5] {paq''batlh 2ed p.90-91:src}, [6]
      {Saarbrücken qepHom''a'' 2023:src}'
    citations:
    - source: tkd
    - source: qepa_2017
      date: '2017'
    - source: kli_mailing_list
      date: '2021-11-11'
    - source: qephom_2021
      date: '2021'
    - source: paqbatlh
      page_start: 90
      page_end: 91
    - source: qephom_2023
      date: '2023'
  translations:
    de:
      definition: Haar (Kopfhaar)
      notes: 'Dies bezieht sich nur auf Haare auf dem Kopf und nicht auf Gesichtshaare
        (siehe {rol:n} und {loch:n}) oder Körperhaare (siehe {pob:n}).[2]


        Tiere haben kein {jIb:n:nolink} sondern {pob:n:nolink}.[3]


        Um zu sagen, dass jemand kahl ist, sagt man einfach {jIb Hutlh:sen@@jIb:n,
        Hutlh:v}.[4]


        Lange Haare können {jIb tIq:n@@jIb:n, tIq:v} sein, was auch die häufigste
        Art ist, über ein einzelnes langes Haar oder lange Strähnen, die nicht mehr
        auf jemandes Kopf sind, zu bezeichnen. Eine übliche Art über eine Langhaarfrisur
        zu sprechen ist {Qa jIb:sen@@Qa:v, jIb:n} (selbst wenn man über eine Perrücke
        trägt).[6]


        Kurzes Haar kann {jIb run:n@@jIb:n, run:v} genannt werden, wobei eine andere,
        vielleicht häufigere, Art ist, zu sagen, dass es geschnitten oder abgeschnitten
        wurde (mit {chIp:v} wie in {jIb chIplu''bogh:n@@jIb:n, chIp:v, -lu'':v, -bogh:v}
        und so weiter). Ein einzelnes kurzes Haar oder eine kurze Strähne, die nicht
        mehr auf dem Kopf ist, wäre {jIb wIl:n@@jIb:n, wIl:v} statt {jIb run:n@@jIb:n,
        run:v}.[6]'
      search_tags: kahl
    fa:
      definition: موی سر
    sv:
      definition: hår (på huvudet)
    ru:
      definition: волосы
    zh_HK:
      definition: 頭髮
    pt:
      definition: cabelo (na cabeça)
    fi:
      definition: hiukset
    fr:
      definition: cheveux
      notes: 'Ce mot se réfère seulement aux cheveux sur la tête et pas aux poils
        du visage (voir {rol:n} et {loch:n}) ou aux poils du corps (voir {pob:n}).[2]


        Les animaux n''ont pas de {jIb:n:nolink}, mais de {pob:n:nolink}.[3]


        Pour dire que quelqu''un est chauve, on dit simplement {jIb Hutlh:sen@@jIb:n,
        Hutlh:v}.[4]


        Les cheveux longs sont {jIb tIq:n@@jIb:n, tIq:v}, ce qui est aussi la manière
        la plus courrante de parler d''un seul cheveu long ou d''une méche de cheveux
        longs qui ne sont plus sur la tête de quelqu''un. Une manière commune de parler
        d''une coiffure à cheveux longs est {Qa jIb:sen@@Qa:v, jIb:n} (même en parlant
        d''une perruque).[6]


        Les cheveux courts sont {jIb run:n@@jIb:n, run:v}, mais une autre locution,
        peut-être plus commune, est de dire que les cheveux ont été coupés (avec {chIp:v}
        comme dans {jIb chIplu''bogh:n@@jIb:n, chIp:v, -lu'':v, -bogh:v} etc). Un
        seul cheveu court ou une mèche de cheveux courts, qui ne sont plus sur la
        tête de quelqu''un, seraient {jIb wIl:n@@jIb:n, wIl:v} plutôt que {jIb run:n@@jIb:n,
        run:v}.[6]'
      search_tags: chauve

entries:

  notes: 'The plural of this pronoun is {maH:n:1h,pro}.


    Verb prefixes when {jIH:n:1h,nolink} is the subject:

    ▶ {jIH:n:1h,nolink}:{pagh:n:1h} = {jI-:v:pref}

    ▶ {jIH:n:1h,nolink}:{SoH:n} = {qa-:v:pref}

    ▶ {jIH:n:1h,nolink}:{ghaH:n}/{''oH:n}/{chaH:n}/{bIH:n} = {vI-:v:pref}


    Verb prefixes when {jIH:n:1h,nolink} is the object:

    ▶ {SoH:n}:{jIH:n:1h,nolink} = {cho-:v:pref}

    ▶ {tlhIH:n}:{jIH:n:1h,nolink} = {tu-:v:pref}

    ▶ {ghaH:n}/{''oH:n}/{chaH:n}/{bIH:n}:{jIH:n:1h,nolink} = {mu-:v:pref}


    The imperative verb prefix when {jIH:n:1h,nolink} is the object is {HI-:v:pref}.'

    ▶ {tlhIngan jIH.:sen}

    ▶ {DaHjaj SuvwI''''e'' jIH.:sen}'

  translations:

      definition: ich
      notes: 'Das Plural dieses Pronomens ist {maH:n:1h,pro}.


        Verbpräfixe wenn {jIH:n:1h,nolink} das Subjekt ist:

        ▶ {jIH:n:1h,nolink}:{pagh:n:1h} = {jI-:v:pref}

        ▶ {jIH:n:1h,nolink}:{SoH:n} = {qa-:v:pref}

        ▶ {jIH:n:1h,nolink}:{tlhIH:n} = {Sa-:v:pref}

        ▶ {jIH:n:1h,nolink}:{ghaH:n}/{''oH:n}/{chaH:n}/{bIH:n} = {vI-:v:pref}


        Verbpräfixe wenn {jIH:n:1h,nolink} das Objekt ist:

        ▶ {SoH:n}:{jIH:n:1h,nolink} = {cho-:v:pref}

        ▶ {tlhIH:n}:{jIH:n:1h,nolink} = {tu-:v:pref}

        ▶ {ghaH:n}/{''oH:n}/{chaH:n}/{bIH:n}:{jIH:n:1h,nolink} = {mu-:v:pref}


        Das Imperativpräfix, wenn {jIH:n:1h,nolink} das Objekt ist, ist {HI-:v:pref}.'
    fa:
      definition: من
    sv:
      definition: jag, mig
    ru:
      definition: я
      notes: 'Множественное число этого местоимения — {maH:n:1h,pro}.


        Глагольные префиксы, когда {jIH:n:1h,nolink} является подлежащим:

        ▶ {jIH:n:1h,nolink}:{pagh:n:1h} = {jI-:v:pref}

        ▶ {jIH:n:1h,nolink}:{SoH:n} = {qa-:v:pref}

        ▶ {jIH:n:1h,nolink}:{tlhIH:n} = {Sa-:v:pref}

        ▶ {jIH:n:1h,nolink}:{ghaH:n}/{''oH:n}/{chaH:n}/{bIH:n} = {vI-:v:pref}


        Глагольные префиксы, когда {jIH:n:1h,nolink} является дополнением:

        ▶ {SoH:n}:{jIH:n:1h,nolink} = {cho-:v:pref}

        ▶ {tlhIH:n}:{jIH:n:1h,nolink} = {tu-:v:pref}

        ▶ {ghaH:n}/{''oH:n}/{chaH:n}/{bIH:n}:{jIH:n:1h,nolink} = {mu-:v:pref}


        Глагольный префикс повелительного наклонения, когда {jIH:n:1h,nolink} является
        дополнением {HI-:v:pref}.'
    zh_HK:
      definition: 我
    pt:
      definition: eu
    fi:
      definition: minä
    fr:
      definition: je, me, moi
      notes: 'Le pluriel de {jIH:n:1h,nolink} est {maH:n:1h,pro}.


        Préfixes verbales quand {jIH:n:1h,nolink} est le sujet:

        ▶ {jIH:n:1h,nolink}:{pagh:n:1h} = {jI-:v:pref}

        ▶ {jIH:n:1h,nolink}:{SoH:n} = {qa-:v:pref}

        ▶ {jIH:n:1h,nolink}:{tlhIH:n} = {Sa-:v:pref}

        ▶ {jIH:n:1h,nolink}:{ghaH:n}/{''oH:n}/{chaH:n}/{bIH:n} = {vI-:v:pref}


        Préfixes verbales quand {jIH:n:1h,nolink} est l''objet:

        ▶ {SoH:n}:{jIH:n:1h,nolink} = {cho-:v:pref}

        ▶ {tlhIH:n}:{jIH:n:1h,nolink} = {tu-:v:pref}

        ▶ {ghaH:n}/{''oH:n}/{chaH:n}/{bIH:n}:{jIH:n:1h,nolink} = {mu-:v:pref}


        Le préfixe impératif quand {jIH:n:1h,nolink} est l''objet est {HI-:v:pref}.'

    zh_HK:
      definition: 查看屏幕
    pt:
      definition: tela de visualização
    fi:
      definition: näyttö, monitori
    fr:
      definition: écran de visualisation
      notes: À noter que {jIH:n:2,nolink} se réfère au dispositif, wandis que {HaSta:n:1}
        se réfère à l'information visuelle qui y est affichée. {HaSta:n:1,nolink}
        et {wIy:n:1} sont entre les affichages qui peuvent se trouver sur un {jIH:n:2,nolink}.

  part_of_speech: n:deriv

  metadata_tags:

  section: main
  definition:
    text: party, celebration (a specific type of Klingon party or celebration)

    - text: celebration

    has been changed for clarity based on the information from {KCD:src}. In {KCD:src},
    Vok says, "The celebration was declared a {lopno':n:nolink}. You have invited
    all the spirits of our Klingon ancestors." This suggests that a {lopno':n:nolink}
    is a type of party or celebration, rather than a specific event.

    raw: '[1] {KGT:src}, [2] {KCD:src}'
    citations:
    - source: kgt
    - source: kcd

      definition: Feier, Fest, "offenes Haus"
    fa:
      definition: حزب، جشن
    sv:
      definition: fest, firande
    ru:
      definition: празднование, званый вечер
    zh_HK:
      definition: 派對、慶祝
    pt:
      definition: festa, celebração
    fi:
      definition: juhlat, festivaali
    fr:
      definition: fête, célébration (un type spécifique de fête ou de célébration
        Klingon)

entry:
  entry_name: lurgh
  slug: lurgh_n
  part_of_speech: n
  pos: n
  status: canonical
  section: main
  definition: direction (spatial)
  see_also: '{Dop:n}, {roDSer:n}, {SInan:n}'
  notes: 'The Klingon compass has three points, rather than four: {chan:n} (east),
    {''ev:n} (northwest), and {tIng:n} (southwest).


    The areas around an object are its {Dung:n} (area above), {bIng:n} (area below),
    {retlh:n} (area beside), {tlhop:n:1} (front), and {''em:n} (behind). Something
    in an object''s {retlh:n:nolink} can be on its {poS:n} (left) or its {nIH:n} (right).
    The area between two objects are their {joj:n} (area between). The area beyond
    an object is its {Hay:n:2h}.


    In standard Klingon, locative nouns follow pronouns, e.g., {jIH tlhop:n:nolink}
    "in front of me". But in the dialect of the Sakrej region ({Sa''Qej Sep:n}), locative
    nouns take pronominal possessive suffixes, e.g., {tlhopwIj:n:nolink} "my area
    in front".[2] However, the directional nouns are an exception to this rule, and
    take possessive suffixes in every known dialect, e.g., {chanwIj:n:nolink} "east
    of me, to my east". If the full pronoun is used with a directional noun, the pronoun
    is emphasized, e.g., {jIH chan:n:nolink} "east of ME, to MY east".[4]


    When referring to one''s left and right sides, possessive suffixes are used. For
    example, one might say {nIHwIj ghop:n@@nIH:n, -wIj:n, ghop:n} to refer to their
    right hand.[5]


    The points in between the three cardinal directions are {tIng chan:n:nolink},
    {''ev chan:n:nolink}, and either {tIng ''ev:n:nolink} or {''ev tIng:n:nolink}.
    {chan:n:nolink} always comes second in such a compound.[3]'
  examples: '

    ▶ {veng chanDaq jIwam.:sen:nolink} "I hunt east of the city."

    ▶ {chan vengDaq jIwam.:sen:nolink} "I hunt in the city in the east."

    ▶ {veng chan yoSDaq jIwam.:sen:nolink} "I hunt in the city''s east (the eastern
    part of the city)."

    ▶ {''evmajDaq jIwampu''.:sen:nolink} "I have hunted northwest of here."  (Northwest
    is relative to the speaker''s location.)

    ▶ {Daqvam ''ev jIwampu''.:sen:nolink} "I have hunted northwest of here." (Northwest
    is relative to a location indicated by the speaker, for example a point on a map.)'
  sources:
    raw: '[1] {TKDA:src}, [2] {KGT p.24:src}, [3] {s.k 1999.11.21:src} (reprinted
      in {HQ 8.4, p.6-8, Dec. 1999:src}), [4] {s.k 1999.12.01:src}, [5] {KLI mailing
      list 2015.08.05:src}'
    citations:
    - source: tkda
    - source: kgt
      page_start: 24
    - source: startrek_klingon
      date: '1999-11-21'
      reprinted_in:
        source: holqed
        page_start: 6
        page_end: 8
        volume: 8
        issue: 4
        date: Dec. 1999
    - source: startrek_klingon
      date: '1999-12-01'
    - source: kli_mailing_list
      date: '2015-08-05'
  translations:
    de:
      definition: Richtung
    fa:
      definition: جهت (فضایی)
    sv:
      definition: riktning (rumslig)
    ru:
      definition: направление (пространственное)
      notes: 'Клингонский компас имеет 3 точки: {chan:n} (восток), {''ev:n} (северо-запад),
        и {tIng:n} (юго-запад).


        Территории вокруг объекта {Dung:n} (територия над), {bIng:n} (территория под),
        {retlh:n} (территория рядом), {tlhop:n:1} (спереди), и {''em:n} (позади).
        Объект {retlh:n:nolink} может быть {poS:n} (слева) или {nIH:n} (справа). Территория
        между двумя объектами их {joj:n} (территория между). Территория за пределами
        объекта {Hay:n:2h}.


        В стандартном клингонском диалекте, локационные существительные следуют за
        местоимениями, {jIH tlhop:n:nolink} "передо мной". Но в диалекте региона Саркедж
        ({Sa''Qej Sep:n}), локационные существительные принимают местоименные притяжательные
        суффиксы, {tlhopwIj:n:nolink} "моя территория передо мной".[2] Тем не менее,
        направленные существительные являются исключением в этом правиле, и принимают
        притяжательные суффиксы в каждом известном диалекте, например {chanwIj:n:nolink}
        "к востоку от меня, ко мне на восток". Если полное местоимение использовано
        с направленным существительным, существительное акцентируется, {jIH chan:n:nolink}
        "к востоку от меня, ко мне на восток".[4]


        При обращении к левой и правой сторонам используются притяжательные суффиксы.
        Например, можно сказать {nIHwIj ghop:n@@nIH:n, -wIj:n, ghop:n} для обозначения
        их правой руки. [5]


        Точки между тремя основными направлениями {tIng chan:n:nolink}, {''ev chan:n:nolink},
        и {tIng ''ev:n:nolink} или {''ev tIng:n:nolink}. {chan:n:nolink} всегда идут
        вторыми в таком соединении.[3]'
      examples: '

        ▶ {veng chanDaq jIwam.:sen:nolink} "Я охочусь к востоку от города."

        ▶ {chan vengDaq jIwam.:sen:nolink} "Я охочусь в городе на востоке."

        ▶ {veng chan yoSDaq jIwam.:sen:nolink} "Я охочусь в восточной части города."

        ▶ {''evmajDaq jIwampu''.:sen:nolink} "Я охотился к северо-западу отсюда(относительно
        местонахождения говорящего)."

        ▶ {Daqvam ''ev jIwampu''.:sen:nolink} "Я охотился к северо-западу отсюда(относительно
        точки, обозначенной говорящим, например на карте)."'
    zh_HK:
      definition: 方向
    pt:
      definition: direção (espacial)
    fi:
      definition: suunta
    fr:
      definition: direction (spatiale)

  notes: 'This is the plural of {jIH:n:1h,pro}.


    Verb prefixes when {maH:n:1h,nolink} is the subject:

    ▶ {maH:n:1h,nolink}:{pagh:n:1h} = {ma-:v:pref}

    ▶ {maH:n:1h,nolink}:{SoH:n} = {pI-:v:pref}

    ▶ {maH:n:1h,nolink}:{tlhIH:n} = {re-:v:pref}

    ▶ {maH:n:1h,nolink}:{ghaH:n}/{''oH:n} = {wI-:v:pref}

    ▶ {maH:n:1h,nolink}:{chaH:n}/{bIH:n} = {DI-:v:pref}


    Verb prefixes when {maH:n:1h,nolink} is the object:

    ▶ {SoH:n}:{maH:n:1h,nolink} = {ju-:v:pref}

    ▶ {tlhIH:n}:{maH:n:1h,nolink} = {che-:v:pref}

    ▶ {ghaH:n}/{''oH:n}/{chaH:n}/{bIH:n}:{maH:n:1h,nolink} = {nu-:v:pref}


    The imperative verb prefix when {maH:n:1h,nolink} is the object is {gho-:v:pref}.'

    citations:

  translations:

      definition: wir, uns

      definition: ما
    sv:
      definition: vi, oss
    ru:
      definition: мы
      notes: 'Единственное число этого местоимения — {jIH:n:1h,pro}.


        Глагольные префиксы, когда {maH:n:1h,nolink} является подлежащим:

        ▶ {maH:n:1h,nolink}:{pagh:n:1h} = {ma-:v:pref}

        ▶ {maH:n:1h,nolink}:{SoH:n} = {pI-:v:pref}

        ▶ {maH:n:1h,nolink}:{tlhIH:n} = {re-:v:pref}

        ▶ {maH:n:1h,nolink}:{ghaH:n}/{''oH:n} = {wI-:v:pref}

        ▶ {maH:n:1h,nolink}:{chaH:n}/{bIH:n} = {DI-:v:pref}


        Глагольные префиксы, когда {maH:n:1h,nolink} является дополнением:

        ▶ {SoH:n}:{maH:n:1h,nolink} = {ju-:v:pref}

  definition: piano (Terran musical instrument)
  see_also: '{HIvje''He:n}'
  notes: There is no instrument like a piano in traditional Klingon culture, but Klingons
    have seen them and use this term to refer to one. This is made up of {may'ron:n},
    a Klingon instrument reminiscent of an accordian, and {raS:n} "table", as if an
    instrument of this type is a {may'ron:n:nolink} built into a table. Even though
    the term ignores the fact that a piano or harpsicord creates sound via vibrating
    strings, it's used for all of these keyboard instruments anyway. If clarification
    is needed, a piano or harpsicord could be a {SIrgh may'ron raS:n@@SIrgh:n, may'ron:n,
    raS:n}. To distinguish a piano from a harpsicord, one could use {SIrgh pangwI'
    may'ron raS:n@@SIrgh:n, pang:v, -wI':v, may'ron:n, raS:n} for harpsicord and {SIrgh
    moqwI' may'ron raS:n@@SIrgh:n, moq:v, -wI':v, may'ron:n, raS:n} for piano. (Occasionally,
    and in appropriate contexts, these could be shortened by leaving out the {may'ron:n}.)
    An organ (if it is necessary to distinguish it from these other instruments) would
    be a {SuS may'ron raS:n@@SuS:n, may'ron:n, raS:n}, even though that's a bit redundant.[1]

    a dialect of Klingon has all but replaced any languages originally spoken.[2,

    In the Morskan dialect, {tlh:sen:nolink} at the end of a syllable is pronounced
    like "ts" (like in "cats"), while at the beginning it is pronounced like {ghl:sen:nolink}.

    while it is not pronounced at all at the ends of syllables. {Q:sen:nolink} at
    the beginning of syllables is pronounced the same as a standard {H:sen:nolink}.[2,
    p.22]

    in a "to be" sentence. When it is present, it serves its usual focusing function.[2,

    has a third-person direct object and a first- or second-person indirect object,

  notes: 'This pronoun is used in a sentence-as-object construction when the second
    sentence has an indefinite third-person subject (i.e., "one" or "someone").


    Sometimes, {''e'':n:pro} with {-lu'':v} is used instead of {net:n:pro,nolink},
    because multiple uses of {-lu'':v:nolink} in a complex sentence refers back to
    the same indefinite subject.[5]'
  examples: '

    (using {X net Y:sen:nolink})

    ▶ {qama''pu'' DIHoH net Sov:sen:nolink} "One knows we kill prisoners."[1, p.66]

    ▶ {Qu''vaD lI'' net tu''bej.:sen} "One certainly finds it useful for the mission."[1,
    p.66]

    ▶ {Duj ghajchugh pagh, beylI''vo'' ''oH Daje'' net chaw''.:sen:nolink} "If (the
    ship is) unowned, you may buy it from the Bank."[3]

    ▶ {DIvI'' rojmab qep ghanglu'' ''e'' nIDlu'', ''ach taH qep.:sen:nolink} "Despite

entry:
  entry_name: ngeng HeH
  slug: ngeng_HeH_n
  part_of_speech: n:deriv
  pos: n
  metadata_tags:
  - deriv
  status: canonical
  section: main
  definition: shore
  see_also: '{qul ngeng:n}'
  notes: 'This refers specifically to the shore of a lake. The shore of an ocean would
    be called a {bIQ''a'' HeH:n}, and so on.


    In the {paq''batlh:src}, the expression {qul ngeng HeH:n:nolink} is used to refer
    to the shore of the {qul ngeng:n} inside {QIStaq:n}, where the environment is
    so hostile to life that not even {tlheng''IQ:n} would grow.'
  components: '{ngeng:n}, {HeH:n}'
  examples: "\n▶ {mob qeylIS:sen:nolink}\n   {ngeng HeHDaq yIt:sen:nolink}\n   {SanDaj\
    \ buS vaj 'It:sen:nolink}\n  \"And Kahless was alone\n   Walking along the shore,\n\
    \   His fate heavy on his shoulders.\"\n  {qul ngeng HeHDaq:sen:nolink}\n   {ba'taHvIS\
    \ qeylIS:sen:nolink}\n   {ghoS SuvwI' qan:sen:nolink}\n  \"Kahless sits at the\
    \ shores\n   Of the lake of fire\n   As an old warrior passes by.\"[2]"
  sources:
    raw: '[1] {paq''batlh 2ed p.86-87:src}'
    citations:
    - source: paqbatlh
      page_start: 86
      page_end: 87
  translations:
    de:
      definition: Ufer
      notes: 'Dies bezieht sich ganz speziell auf das Ufer eines Sees. Das Ufer eines
        Ozeans wäre {bIQ''a'' HeH:n}, und so weiter.


        Im {paq''batlh:src}, wird der Ausdruck {qul ngeng HeH:n:nolink} für das Ufer
        des {qul ngeng:n} im {QIStaq:n} benutzt, wo die Umwelt so lebensfeindlich
        ist, dass nicht einmal {tlheng''IQ:n} dort wächst.'
      examples: "\n▶ {mob qeylIS:sen:nolink}\n   {ngeng HeHDaq yIt:sen:nolink}\n \
        \  {SanDaj buS vaj 'It:sen:nolink}\n  \"Und Kahless war aleine\n   Lief am\
        \ Ufer entlang,\n   Sein schweres Shcicksal auf den Schultern.\"\n  {qul ngeng\
        \ HeHDaq:sen:nolink}\n   {ba'taHvIS qeylIS:sen:nolink}\n   {ghoS SuvwI' qan:sen:nolink}\n\
        \  \"Kahless sitz am Ufer\n   Am See des Feuers\n   Als ein alter Krieger\
        \ vorbeikommt.\"[2]"
    fa:
      definition: ساحل دریاچه
    sv:
      definition: strand, kust
    ru:
      definition: берег
    zh_HK:
      definition: 湖邊
    pt:
      definition: costa
    fi:
      definition: (järven) ranta
    fr:
      definition: rive (d'un lac)
      notes: 'Ceci se réfère spécifiquement à la rive d''un lac. La rive d''un océan
        serait appelé {bIQ''a'' HeH:n}, etc.


        Dans le {paq''batlh:src}, l''expression {qul ngeng HeH:n:nolink} est utilisé
        pour parler de la rive du {qul ngeng:n} dans le {QIStaq:n}, où l''environnement
        est si hostile à la vie que même {tlheng''IQ:n} n''y croît pas.'
      examples: "\n▶ {mob qeylIS:sen:nolink}\n   {ngeng HeHDaq yIt:sen:nolink}\n \
        \  {SanDaj buS vaj 'It:sen:nolink}\n  \"Et Kahless était seul\n   Il marcha\
        \ le long de la rive,\n   Son sort est lourd sur ses épaules.\"\n  {qul ngeng\
        \ HeHDaq:sen:nolink}\n   {ba'taHvIS qeylIS:sen:nolink}\n   {ghoS SuvwI' qan:sen:nolink}\n\
        \  \"Kahless est assis sur la rive\n   Du lac de feu\n   Quand un vieux guerrier\
        \ passe.\"[2]"

entry:
  entry_name: ngevwI'
  slug: ngevwI'_n
  part_of_speech: n:being,deriv
  pos: n
  pos_subtype: being
  metadata_tags:
  - deriv
  status: canonical
  section: main
  definition: seller
  see_also: '{Suy:n}, {Hergh ngevwI'':n}'
  notes: 'This word refers to a person, although it can be used to translate the word
    "store" or "shop" in context, in the sense that in Klingon, one says that one
    is going to the pharmacist rather than to the pharmacy.


    In {TNK:src}, "Where is the shop?" is translated as {nuqDaq ghaH ngevwI''''e''?:sen:nolink}
    (literally, "Where is the seller?") Note that {ghaH:n} is used rather than {''oH:n}.'
  search_tags: store, shop
  sources:
    raw: '[1] {TNK:src}'
    citations:
    - source: tnk
  translations:
    de:
      definition: Verkäufer
      notes: 'Dieses Wort bezieht sich auf eine Person, kann aber auch benutzt werden,
        um das Wort "Geschäft" im Kontext zu übersetzen, im Sinne, dass man auf Klingonisch
        sagt, dass man zum Apotheker geht und nicht zur Apotheke.


        In {TNK:src}, wird "Wo ist das Geschäft?" als {nuqDaq ghaH ngevwI''''e''?:sen:nolink}
        (wörtlich, "Wo ist der Verkäufer?") übersetzt. Merke, dass {ghaH:n} statt
        {''oH:n} benutzt wird.'
      search_tags: Geschäft, Laden
    fa:
      definition: فروشنده
    sv:
      definition: säljare
    ru:
      definition: продавец, торговец
      notes: 'Это слово относится к лицу, хотя может быть переведено, как магазин.


        В {TNK:src}, "Где находится магазин?" переведено, как {nuqDaq ghaH ngevwI''''e''?:sen:nolink}
        Заметьте, что {ghaH:n} предпочтительней, чем {''oH:n}.'
    zh_HK:
      definition: 賣家
    pt:
      definition: vendedor
    fi:
      definition: myyjä
    fr:
      definition: vendeur
      notes: 'Ce mot se réfère à une personne, mais il peut être utilisé pour traduire
        le mot "magasin" en contexte, dans le sens qu''en klingon, on dit d''aller
        chez le pharmacien plutôt qu''à la pharmacie.


        Dans {TNK:src}, "Où est le magasin?" est traduit par {nuqDaq ghaH ngevwI''''e''?:sen:nolink}
        (littéralement, "Où est le vendeur?") À noter que {ghaH:n} est utilisé plutôt
        que {''oH:n}.'
      search_tags: magasin

entry:
  entry_name: ngIq
  slug: ngIq_n
  part_of_speech: n
  pos: n
  status: canonical
  section: main
  definition:
    text: a single one, each one
    parts:
    - text: a single one
    - text: each one
  see_also: '{ghIq:adv}, {Hoch:n}, {''op:n}'
  notes: 'This noun indicates that a single thing is being considered apart from others,
    or that a sequence of identical things is considered one after another. Like {Hoch:n}
    and {''op:n}, it precedes what it modifies.[4]


    {ngIq:n:nolink} is always followed by a noun which is not explicitly plural. In
    contexts where it refers to multiple things, it can be translated as "each X".
    When {Hoch:n:nolink} precedes a noun which isn''t explicitly plural, it also means
    "each X". The difference is that {Hoch:n:nolink} focuses on things as members
    of a group, whereas {ngIq:n:nolink} focuses on the individual things. It''s a
    subtle difference, but a difference nonetheless. In such contexts, {ngIq:n:nolink}
    has a sequential meaning (whereas {Hoch:n:nolink} does not).[4]


    In some contexts, {ngIq:n:nolink} can be translated as "single" or "individual",
    but it always implies that there are (or could be) other similar things. For example,
    {ngIq tonSaw'':n:nolink} means "one single move" in the sense of "one single move
    out of several". That is, {ngIq:n:nolink} is used to focus on one move in particular.[4]'
  hidden_notes: 'In an article writtten for the {Saarbrücken qepHom''a'' 2017:src}
    booklet, MO wrote that "The description of {ngIq:n:nolink} in {boQwI'':n:nolink}
    is pretty good". This is preserved in the first paragraph in the notes.


    "Unique".'

    \  \"In one single move, he removed the hearts,\n   In one single move, he restored\
    \ his honor,\n   In one single move, the battle was done.\"[2, p.166-167]\n▶ {ngIq\
    \ tonSaw' lo':sen:nolink}\n   {SaD law' San chenmoH qeylIS:sen:nolink}\n   {wej\

entries:
- entry_name: pa'
  slug: pa'_n_1
  part_of_speech: n:1,klcp1
  pos: n
  homophone: 1
  metadata_tags:
  - klcp1
  status: canonical
  section: main
  definition:
    text: room, enclosed area, chamber
    parts:
    - text: room
    - text: enclosed area
    - text: chamber
  see_also: '{qach:n}'
  notes: 'This word is homophonous with {pa'':n:2}. However, {pa''Daq:n:nolink} unambiguously
    means "in the room".


    The {bIS''ub:n} of a {pa'':n:1h,nolink} is its {rav:n:1}, and its {''aqroS:n:1}
    is its {rav''eq:n}. If the {pa'':n:1h,nolink} is in the top story of a {qach:n},
    then its {rav''eq:n} is called its {pa'' beb:n}. The walls of a {pa'':n:1h,nolink}
    are {tlhoy'':n}; if the other side of a wall is {Hur:n:1}, then the wall is also
    called a {pa'' reD:n}. The word {tlhoy'':n} can refer to any side of a room; a
    ceiling/floor between stories is called a {tlhoy'' SaS:n}.'
  hidden_notes: This word is defined as "room" in {TKD:src}, as "enclosed area" in
    {KGT:src}, and as "chamber" in {BoP:src} (see {cha'puj pa':n}).
  examples: '

    ▶ {ghorgh pa''wIjDaq jIchegh?:sen}

    ▶ {pa''vo'' pagh leghlu''.:sen}

    ▶ {pa''vo'' yIjaH!:sen}'
  sources:
    raw: '[1] {TKD:src}, [2] {KGT:src}, [3] {BoP:src}, [4] {HQ 8.3, p.2, Sep. 1999:src}'
    citations:
    - source: tkd
    - source: kgt
    - source: bop
    - source: holqed
      page_start: 2
      volume: 8
      issue: 3
      date: Sep. 1999
  translations:
    de:
      definition: Raum, Zimmer, Kammer
    fa:
      definition: اتاق، محوطه محوطه، محوطه
    sv:
      definition: rum, kammare, inhägnat område
    ru:
      definition: комната, помещение, пространство, закрытое помещение, камера, палата
      notes: 'Слово является омофоном для {pa'':n:2}. Однако, {pa''Daq:n:nolink} однозначно
        значит "в комнате".


        Слово {bIS''ub:n} для {pa'':n:1h,nolink} будет {rav:n:1}, а {''aqroS:n:1}
        будет {rav''eq:n}. Если {pa'':n:1h,nolink} наверху {qach:n}, тогда этот {rav''eq:n}
        называется {pa'' beb:n}. Стены для {pa'':n:1h,nolink} будут {tlhoy'':n}; Если
        другая сторона стены будет {Hur:n:1}, тогда такая стена называется {pa'' reD:n}.
        Слово {tlhoy'':n} может относиться к любой стороне комнаты; пол/потолок между
        этажами называется {tlhoy'' SaS:n}.'
    zh_HK:
      definition: 房間、封閉區域、房間
    pt:

    fi:
      definition: huone, kammio, suljettu alue
    fr:

entry:
  entry_name: pIqaD
  slug: pIqaD_n
  part_of_speech: n
  pos: n
  status: canonical
  section: main
  definition: Klingon writing system
  see_also: '{ghItlhmeH Ho''DoS:n}, {ngutlh:n}, {Degh:n:1}'
  notes: Little is known about how {pIqaD:n:nolink} works, except that it is not an
    alphabet.[2]
  hidden_notes: 'If interpreted as a sentence, {pIqaD:sen@@pI-:v, qaD:v} literally
    means "we challenge you".


    Prior to {DSC:src}, the {pIqaD:n:nolink} seen in the shows, movies, and videogames
    were arranged based on aesthetics and had no relation to the language. This allowed
    the costume and set designers to freely create decorative text and reuse templates.
    Some of the same sequences of symbols were even used to mean different things
    in different contexts. In {DSC:src}, both within the show itself and in promotional
    posters and videos released prior to its debut, Klingon is written in {pIqaD:n:nolink}
    treating the symbols as an alphabet. The mapping between the twenty-six symbols
    and Okrand''s Latin transcription has a one-to-one grapheme-phoneme correspondence
    (e.g., so that {tlh:sen:nolink} is written as one symbol), and originated from
    an unknown source at Paramount and was popularised by the Klingon Language Institute.
    There is no official explanation for why {pIqaD:n:nolink} appears to be an alphabet
    in {DSC:src}.'
  sources:
    raw: '[1] {TKD p.11:src}, [2] {msn 1997.10.17:src}'

entry:
  entry_name: Qa'Hom
  slug: Qa'Hom_n
  part_of_speech: n:anim
  pos: n
  categories:
  - anim
  status: canonical
  section: main
  definition: type of animal (cowardly animal similar to {Qa':n:1} but smaller, mistaken
    for a bird by some)
  notes: 'This literally means "little {Qa'':n:1,nolink}", though a {Qa''Hom:n:nolink}
    is not a young {Qa'':n:1,nolink}, which is a larger, more dangerous animal. However,
    it does bear a vague resemblance. This word is also used as an epithet to denote
    someone who is weak and scared easily, and whom there is no honour in killing.[2]


    This animal does not make a ruckus at dawn, unlike the {jajlo'' Qa'':n}. It is
    mistaken for a bird by some.[3]


    Watch Gowron say this: {YouTube video:url:http://youtu.be/SIpF7Zak6CY}'
  hidden_notes: 'This word appears in the "Curses" section of the {KCD:src} Language
    Lab. In the introduction to the holodeck part of the game, it is used in a derogatory
    manner by Gowron to refer to the player character. Gowron says that there is no
    honour in killing a {Qa''Hom:n:nolink}, but that after the player has finished
    the holodeck adventure, they will no longer be as weak as a {Qa''Hom:n:nolink},
    and then "it will be an honour to kill you".[2]


    The English text in {KCD:src} for this word reads "little animal (e.g., Ligonian
    titmouse)", and it is accompanied by an image of a hedgehog. Presumably, whoever
    selected the image did not realise that a "titmouse" is a kind of bird, and not
    a kind of mouse (which a hedgehog also is not). The audio (which is spoken by
    Marc Okrand) addresses this discrepancy by implying that it resembles a titmouse
    only in its unimportance: "The translation ''titmouse'' is really only an approximation
    of what this word means. A {Qa''Hom:n:nolink} is a small animal considered rather
    insignificant."


    This error is alluded to again in {HQ 10.4:src}, which states some people have
    confused it with a bird for reasons unknown to Maltz. In a personal message to
    {Quvar:n:name} in May 2021, Marc Okrand confirmed that the image is correct and
    that the text is in error, i.e., the {Qa''Hom:n:nolink} resembles a Terran hedgehog.


    Even though {KCD:src} was published before {KGT:src}, the book is listed as the
    first source since it is where the definition comes from.'
  sources:
    raw: '[1] {KGT:src}, [2] {KCD:src}, [3] {HQ 10.4, Dec. 2001:src}'
    citations:
    - source: kgt
    - source: kcd
    - source: holqed

      date: Dec. 2001

entry:
  entry_name: qa'vam
  slug: qa'vam_n
  part_of_speech: n
  pos: n
  status: canonical
  section: main
  definition:
    text: Genesis, "Big Bang"
    parts:
    - text: Genesis
    - text: '"Big Bang"'
  see_also: '{bI''reS:n}'
  notes: 'This is the Klingon code name for the Federation''s Genesis weapons research
    project.[2]


    The word itself means "origin of everything" or "start of it all" or the like,
    and refers to the beginning of the universe. Unlike its English translation, the
    Klingon term doesn''t contain the notion of an explosion.[3]'
  hidden_notes: Maltz said that it's possible to say {qa'vam nger:sen:nolink} "Big
    Bang Theory", but it sounded weird to him, since {qa'vam:n:nolink} is not a theory.[3]
  examples: '

    ▶ {qa''vam De'' vIje'' rIntaH.:sen}[2]'
  search_tags: Big Bang
  sources:
    raw: '[1] {TKD:src}, [2] {Star Trek III:src}, [3] {KLI mailing list 2015.03.16:src}'
    citations:
    - source: tkd
    - source: star_trek_iii
    - source: kli_mailing_list
      date: '2015-03-16'
  translations:
    de:
      definition: Genesis, "Urknall"
    fa:
      definition: پیدایش، "بیگ بنگ"
    sv:
      definition: Genesis
    ru:
      definition: Генезис, "Большой взрыв"
      notes: 'Это Клингонское кодовое имя для исследовательского проекта оружия Федерации.[2]


        Слово само по себе означает "источник всего" или "начало начал" или что-то
        подобное, и относится к началу вселенной.[3]'
    zh_HK:
      definition: 創世、《大爆炸》
      notes: In the subtitles for {Star Trek III:src}, Project Genesis is translated
        as "創世計劃".[2]
    pt:
      definition: Gênesis, "Big Bang"
    fi:
      definition: maailman synty, alkuräjähdys
    fr:
      definition: Genèse, "Big Bang"

entries:
- entry_name: QaS
  slug: QaS_n_1
  part_of_speech: n:being,inhpl,1h
  pos: n
  pos_subtype: being
  homophone: 1
  categories:
  - inhpl
  status: canonical
  section: main
  definition:
    text: troops, troop member
    parts:
    - text: troops
    - text: troop member
    dedup: true
  see_also: '{beq:n}, {negh:n}, {yaS:n:1h}'
  notes: 'The meaning of this word is like {negh:n}, but it excludes officers ({yaS:n:1h}).
    The highest ranks of {QaS:n:1h,nolink} are:

    ▶ {bu'':n} "sergeant"

    ▶ {Da'':n} "corporal"


    It''s possible that this word can be used to refer to a single troop member.[2,
    p.51]


    In {Klingon Monopoly:src}, {tlhIngan QaS:n:nolink} is the unit of currency used
    in the game. From this game, we have the examples {"GO" DajuSDI'' cha''vatlh QaS
    yItlhap:sen:nolink} and {wa''vatlh QaS yItlhap:sen:nolink}. Note that the singular
    prefix {yI-:v} is used even though {QaS:n:1h,nolink} is an inherently plural noun
    whose members are being counted.[3]'
  hidden_notes: This was defined as "troops" in {TKD:src}. It is glossed as "troop
    member" in passing on {KGT p.51:src}.
  sources:
    raw: '[1] {TKD:src}, [2] {KGT:src}, [3] {Klingon Monopoly:src}'
    citations:
    - source: tkd
    - source: kgt
    - source: klingon_monopoly
  translations:
    de:
      definition: Mannschaften (Soldaten ohne Offiziere), Mitglieder der Mannschaftsdienstgrade
    fa:
      definition: نیروهای
    sv:
      definition: trupper
    ru:
      definition: Войска
      notes: 'Значение данного слова подобно {negh:n}, но исключает офицеров ({yaS:n:1h}).
        Высшие ранги {QaS:n:1h,nolink} это:

        ▶ {bu'':n} "Сержант"

        ▶ {Da'':n} "Прапорщик"


        Возможно, что это слово может использоваться для упоминания одного члена из
        войск.[2, p.51]


        В {Klingon Monopoly:src}, {tlhIngan QaS:n:nolink} является единицей валюты,
        используемой в игре. Из этой игры есть примеры {"Вперед!!!!" DajuSDI'' cha''vatlh
        QaS yItlhap:sen:nolink} и {wa''vatlh QaS yItlhap:sen:nolink}. Заметьте, что
        префикс {yI-:v} используется хотя {QaS:n:1h,nolink} в сущности является существительным
        во множественном числе, чьи члены являются исчислимыми.[3]'
    zh_HK:
      definition: 軍隊
    pt:
      definition: tropas
    fi:
      definition: (sota)joukot; miehistö (ei-upseerit)
      search_tags: sotajoukot, joukot
    fr:
      definition: troupes, membre de la troupe

    The transcription system used to write Klingon in the Roman (English) alphabet

    a rough guide, IPA phonetic symbols are shown between a pair of slashes following
    the Roman letter or letters used to transcribe each sound.


    The consonants {b:sen:nolink} /b/, {ch:sen:nolink} /ʧ/, {j:sen:nolink} /d͡ʒ/,

    /j/ are pronounced more or less as in American English.


    {D:sen:nolink} /ɖ/ and {S:sen:nolink} /ʂ/ are retroflex, that is, they are pronounced
    with the tongue touching the roof of the mouth.


    {gh:sen:nolink} /ɣ/ is similar to {H:sen:nolink} (see below), but voiced. It sounds
    somewhat like gargling.


    {H:sen:nolink} /x/ is like the "ch" in the Scottish word "loch" or the name of
    the German composer "Bach".


    {ng:sen:nolink} /ŋ/ is the same sound as is found at the end of the English words
    "sing" or "thing", but in Klingon it can come at the beginning of words.


    {q:sen:nolink} /qʰ/ is like the English "k", but with the tongue reaching for
    or touching the uvula. It sounds a little bit like you''re choking.


    {Q:sen:nolink} /q͡χ/ is similar to a combination of {q:sen:nolink} and {H:sen:nolink},
    and sounds like you''re really choking and trying to dislodge food stuck in your
    throat.


    The Klingon {r:sen:nolink} /r/ is slightly trilled or rolled.


    {tlh:sen:nolink} /t͡ɬ/ is found in some Native American languages, and is produced
    by putting your tongue in the position to say {t:sen:nolink}, then forcing air
    through the sides of your mouth as if to say {l:sen:nolink}.


    The glottal stop {'':sen:nolink} /ʔ/ ({qaghwI'':n:nolink}) is a slight pause or
    catch in the throat, like between the two syllables of "uh-oh".


    The vowel {a:sen:nolink} /ɑ/ sounds like the "a" in "psalm" or "father".


    The vowel {e:sen:nolink} /ɛ/ sounds like the "e" in "bed" or "egg".


    The vowel {I:sen:nolink} /ɪ/ sounds like the "i" in "bit" or "misfit". Note that
    it is always written as a capital letter.


    The vowel {o:sen:nolink} /o/ sounds like the "o" in "note" or "mosaic".


    The vowel {u:sen:nolink} /u/ sounds like the "u" in "prune" or "food".


    The diphthongs {aw:sen:nolink}, {ew:sen:nolink}, {Iw:sen:nolink}, {ay:sen:nolink},
    {ey:sen:nolink}, {Iy:sen:nolink}, {oy:sen:nolink}, and {uy:sen:nolink} are possible,
    and sound essentially like their components. Note that {ay:sen:nolink} rhymes
    with English "why" or "my", whereas {ey:sen:nolink} rhymes with "way" or "may".

    and the names of the vowels consist of the sound preceded by {'':sen:nolink} and
    followed by {t:sen:nolink}. The glottal stop is an exception, being called the

        парами слешей после Римской буквы или букв, что используются для расшифровки
        каждого звука.

        /pʰ/, {t:sen:nolink} /tʰ/, {v:sen:nolink} /v/, {w:sen:nolink} /w/, и {y:sen:nolink}

    (see {qubbID:n:2}).[2]'

    equal to half ({bID:n}) a cubit.

entry:
  entry_name: SaD
  slug: SaD_n
  part_of_speech: n:num
  pos: n
  pos_subtype: num
  status: canonical
  section: main
  definition: thousand (number-forming element)
  see_also: '{mI'':n}, {vatlh:n:num}, {netlh:n:num}'
  notes: 'Another variant of this word which is used with roughly equal frequency
    is {SanID:n:num,nolink}.


    This is a number-forming element, and not itself a number. The number 1000 (one
    thousand) is {wa''SaD:n:num,nolink} in Klingon.


    Note that Klingon has number-forming elements for "ten thousand" ({netlh:n:num})
    and "hundred thousand" ({bIp:n:num}) which are independent of the word for "thousand".


    While {SaD law'':n:nolink} is a grammatical expression, {SaDmey:n:nolink} is not.[3]'
  examples: "\n▶ {ngIq tonSaw' lo':sen:nolink}\n   {SaD law' San chenmoH qeylIS:sen:nolink}\n\
    \   {wej boghbogh nuvpu' San chenmoH:sen:nolink}\n  \"In one single move,\n  \
    \ Kahless decided the fate\n   Of thousands, and those to come.\"[2, p.166-167]\n\
    ▶ {tlheDDI' quvmoHmeH:sen:nolink}\n   {veng HeHDaq lutlha':sen:nolink}\n   {SaD\
    \ law' nuvpu':sen:nolink}\n  \"Thousands followed him\n   To the edge of the city,\n\
    \   To bid him farewell.\"[2, p.176-177]"
  sources:
    raw: '[1] {TKD:src}, [2] {paq''batlh 2ed:src}, [3] {Saarbrücken qepHom''a'' 2019:src}'
    citations:
    - source: tkd
    - source: paqbatlh
    - source: qephom_2019
      date: '2019'
  translations:
    de:
      definition: Tausend (Zahlenbildungsmorphem)
      notes: 'Eine andere Variante dieses Worts, die mit recht gleicher Häufigkeit
        verwendet wird, ist {SanID:n:num,nolink}.


        Dies ist ein zahlenbildendes Morphem oder Element und nicht eine Zahl an sich.
        Die Zahl 1000 (eintausend) ist {wa''SaD:n:num,nolink} auf klingonisch.


        Merke, dass die klingonischen zahlenbildenden Elemente für "zehntausend" ({netlh:n:num})
        und "hunderttausend" ({bIp:n:num}) unabhängig von dem Wort für "tausend" sind.


        Während {SaD law'':n:nolink} ein grammatikalisch korrekter Ausdruck ist, ist
        {SaDmey:n:nolink} es nicht.[3]'
      examples: "\n▶ {ngIq tonSaw' lo':sen:nolink}\n   {SaD law' San chenmoH qeylIS:sen:nolink}\n\
        \   {wej boghbogh nuvpu' San chenmoH:sen:nolink}\n  \"In einer Bewegung,\n\
        \   Besiegelte Kahless das Schicksal\n   Von Tausenden und ihren Nachfahren.\"\
        [2, p.166-167]\n▶ {tlheDDI' quvmoHmeH:sen:nolink}\n   {veng HeHDaq lutlha':sen:nolink}\n\
        \   {SaD law' nuvpu':sen:nolink}\n  \"Tausende folgten ihm\n   Zum Rand der\
        \ Stadt,\n   Um sich zu verabschieden.\"[2, p.176-177]"
    fa:
      definition: هزار
    sv:
      definition: tusen (nummerbildande element)
    ru:
      definition: тысяча
    zh_HK:
      definition: 千
    pt:
      definition: mil
    fi:
      definition: tuhat
    fr:
      definition: mille (morphème formant un nombre)
      notes: 'Une autre variante de ce mot, utilisé avec fréquence assez similaire,
        est {SanID:n:num,nolink}.


        Ceci est un morphème formant un nombre et pas un nombre en soi. Le nombre
        1000 (mille) est {wa''SaD:n:num,nolink} en klingon.


        À noter que les éléments formants les nombres "dix mille" ({netlh:n:num})
        et "cent mille" ({bIp:n:num}) sont indépendents du mot pour "mille".


        Tandis que {SaD law'':n:nolink} est une expression grammaticalement correcte,
        {SaDmey:n:nolink} ne l''est pas.[3]'
      examples: "\n▶ {ngIq tonSaw' lo':sen:nolink}\n   {SaD law' San chenmoH qeylIS:sen:nolink}\n\
        \   {wej boghbogh nuvpu' San chenmoH:sen:nolink}\n  \"Dans un seul mouvement,\n\
        \   Kahless decida le sort\n   De milliers, et ceux à venir.\"[2, p.166-167]\n\
        ▶ {tlheDDI' quvmoHmeH:sen:nolink}\n   {veng HeHDaq lutlha':sen:nolink}\n \
        \  {SaD law' nuvpu':sen:nolink}\n  \"Des milliers le suivèrent\n   Au bord\
        \ de la ville,\n   Pour lui dire au revoir.\"[2, p.176-177]"

  slug: SIrlop_n_1
  part_of_speech: n:1
  pos: n
  homophone: 1
  status: canonical
  section: main
  definition: constant (mathematics, science)
  notes: This is a value that never changes.[1]
  hidden_notes: Reverse of "Polaris", the North Star. In {Star Trek VI:src}, General
    Chang quotes Julius Caesar III.i, "I am constant as the Northern Star".
  sources:
    raw: '[1] {Saarbrücken qepHom''a'' 2024:src}'
    citations:
    - source: qephom_2024
      date: '2024'
  translations:
    de:
      definition: Konstante (Mathematik, Naturwissenschaften)
      notes: Dies ist ein Wert, der sich nie ändert.[1]
    fa:
      definition: ثابت (ریاضیات، علوم)
    sv:
      definition: konstant (matematik, naturvetenskap)
    ru:
      definition: константа (математика, естествознание)
    zh_HK:
      definition: 常數（數學、科學）
    pt:
      definition: constante (matemática, ciências)
    fi:
      definition: (matemaattinen tai luonnontieteellinen) vakio
    fr:
      definition: constante (mathématiques, sciences)
      notes: Ceci est une valeur qui ne change jamais.[1]
- entry_name: SIrlop
  slug: SIrlop_n_2
  part_of_speech: n:2
  pos: n
  homophone: 2
  status: canonical
  section: main
  definition: unit (of measure)
  notes: This is the general term like in English "unit of length" or "unit of measure".
    For example, when a person says "It's five long", someone might reply with "Identify
    the unit!"[1]
  sources:
    raw: '[1] {Saarbrücken qepHom''a'' 2025:src}'
    citations:
    - source: qephom_2025
      date: '2025'
  translations:
    de:
      definition: Maßeinheit
      notes: Dies ist der allgemeine Begriff wie auf Deutsch "Längeneinheit" oder
        "Maßeinheit". Zum Beispiel, wenn jemand sagt "Es ist fünf lang", könnte jemand
        mit "Identifiziere die Einheit!" antworten.[1]
    fa:
      definition: واحد اندازه گیری
    sv:
      definition: måttenhet
    ru:
      definition: единица (меры)
    zh_HK:
      definition: （計量單位）
    pt:
      definition: unidade (de medida)
    fi:
      definition: yksikkö (mittayksikkö)
    fr:
      definition: unité (de mesure)
      notes: Ceci est le terme général comme en français "unité de longueur" ou "unité
        de mesure". Par exemple, si quelqu'un dit "Il est cinq de long" on pourrait
        répondre par "Identifie l'unité!"[1]

  examples: "\n▶ {So'wI':sen:nolink}\n   {Hoch tlhIngan DujDaq So'wI' jomlu'. puvtaHbogh\
    \ Duj ngabmoHlaw' So'wI'. boq lucherDI' tlhIngan wo' romuluS Hov wo' je So'wI'\

    \ wa' vI' jav Dujvam 'aghlu'pu' 'ach Qaw'lu'pu'.:sen:nolink}\n  \"Cloaking Device\n\

  synonyms: '{ghul:n}'
  antonyms: '{retlaw:n}'
  see_also: '{taw'':v}'
  notes: 'This is a general term for any kind of raised profile or relief, such as
    the ridges on the fingertips, the patterns on a car tire, or the profile of a
    shoe. It cannot be used for the ridges on the forehead, though.


    This word is contrasted with {vem:n}, which is the trace left behind when someone
    touches something. For example, compare {nItlh Su''nIm:n} "fingerprint" (ridges
    on fingertip) with {nItlh Su''nIm vem:n} "fingerprint" (mark left behind after
    touching).


    When used to refer to the fingerprint, etc., as a body part, this word takes the
    plural suffix {-Du'':n}. (Otherwise, it takes the suffix {-mey:n}.)


    In the following examples, the specific finger or toe name can be used instead
    of {nItlh:n} and {yaD:n:1}.'
  hidden_notes: The object leaving a pattern is often the "negative" image of the
    pattern.

    ▶ {yaD Su''nIm:n@@yaD:n:1, Su''nIm:n} toe print (ridges on toe tip)

    ▶ {bem Su''nIm:n@@bem:n, Su''nIm:n} footprint (patterns on sole)

entry:
  entry_name: taymey
  slug: taymey_n
  part_of_speech: n
  pos: n
  status: canonical
  section: main
  definition: section of a book or play separate from main portion of the work
  notes: This refers to a section of a book or play or the like that is separate from
    the main portion of the work. It's seldom used without {bI'reS:n} or {bertlham:n},
    except when already established by prior context. Despite its description, {taymey:n}
    is not used for the appendix of a work (for which see {HommaH:n}). A {taymey:n:nolink}
    contextualizes the main work, whereas an appendix is considered supplemental.
    This word may be a remnant of the way stories used to be told orally, since they'd
    begin and end with some sort of ritual ({tay:n:2}), the details of which are lost.
    Even though {taymey:n:nolink} appears to end with the plural suffix {-mey:n},
    it is a frozen form and is considered singular. Thus, it's possible to say {taymeymey:n@@taymey:n,
    -mey:n} should the need arise.[1]
  examples: '{bI''reS taymey:n}, {bertlham taymey:n}'
  sources:

    invitation reads:

    ▶ {tera'' poH jaj wa'', jar wa'', jaj loSDIch, DIS wa''-Hut-Hut-chorgh. HovpoHvetlh
    latlh nab yIHutlh.:sen:nolink} "Save this Stardate: Sunday, January 4, 1998".[1]


    Based on the information on the invitation, when telling an Earth date:

    ▶ the days of the week are mapped to their Klingon analogues (see under {Hogh:n});

    ▶ {jar:n} followed by a number labels the month, starting with January, {jar wa'':n:nolink};

    ▶ the day of the month is given as an ordinal, {jaj loSDIch:n:nolink} "the fourth
    day";

    ▶ the year is specified by giving its digits after the word {DIS:n:2}.[1]


    The Terran months are:

    ▶ {jar wa'':n:nolink} "January"

    ▶ {jar cha'':n:nolink} "February"

    ▶ {jar wej:n:nolink} "March"

    ▶ {jar loS:n:nolink} "April"

    ▶ {jar wa''maH:n:nolink} "October"

    how people will live "in the future" (not at a specific point in the future, but

    not to the Klingon language (for which see {tlhIngan Hol:n}). In Klingon, unlike
    in Federation Standard, the name of a language is not simply the name of the people
    who speak it, but must be an identifier followed by the word {Hol:n}.


    There is an idiom, {Hem; tlhIngan rur@@Hem:v, tlhIngan:n, rur:v}.'
  hidden_notes: The TKD entry says only "Klingon". The "(person)" annotation has been
    added to distinguish this entry from "Klingon (language)", and to make it consistent
    with the entry for "Vulcan (person)", etc.

    ▶ {bogh tlhInganpu'', SuvwI''pu'' moj, Hegh.:sen}'
  sources:
    raw: '[1] {TKD:src}'
    citations:
    - source: tkd
  translations:

      definition: Klingone
      notes: 'Merke, dass dies sich auf eine klingonische Person oder klingonsiche
        Leute bezieht, aber nicht auf die klingonische Sprache (dafür, siehe {tlhIngan
        Hol:n}). Im Klingonischen, im Gegensatz zum Föderationsstandard, ist der Name
        einer Sprache nicht einfach der Name der Leute, die sie sprechen, aber muss
        von dem Wort {Hol:n} gefolgt werden.

    fr:

        mais pas à la langue klingonne (pour ça, voir {tlhIngan Hol:n}). En klingon,

    of) a fingerprint, tire tracks, or the pattern in the dirt that results from stepping

    This word is contrasted with {Su''nIm:n} which refers to the pattern that makes

    detailed which leaves the {vem:n:nolink}. For example, compare {nItlh Su''nIm:n}
    "fingerprint" (ridges on fingertip) with {nItlh Su''nIm vem:n} "fingerprint" (mark
    left behind after touching).


    Note that an intentionally produced, stamp-like image is a {yang:n}.


    In the following examples, the specific finger or toe name can be used instead
    of {nItlh:n} (or {yaD:n:1}).'

entry:
  entry_name: wev
  slug: wev_n
  part_of_speech: n
  pos: n
  status: canonical
  section: main
  definition: row (in a table or spreadsheet)
  antonyms: '{war:n}'
  see_also: '{wa''chaw:n}, {tlhat:n}, {lanSoy:n}, {wIyqap:n}'
  notes: 'Besides being used for a row in a grid (as in a spreadsheet or other graphic
    representation), this can also be used for physical things if the overall configuration
    is (or might be) grid-like and there are (or might be) other rows, not just one.
    For example, this would be used for rows of corn or rows of trees growing in a
    field on a farm. It could still be used if there''s only one row in a situation
    where typically there are more (or it wouldn''t be surprising if there were more).
    If it''s unclear in a situation whether more than one row is expected or typical,
    {wIyqap:n:nolink} is probably the right choice.


    The word {mIr:n:1} can be used as a slang term for this, if things are clear.'
  hidden_notes: 'From the term "warp and weft" in weaving. See also {war:n}.


    This was originally defined as "row (in a table or spreadsheet)" at {Saarbrücken
    qepHom''a'' 2015:src} but was expanded to include physical things later.[2]'
  sources:
    raw: '[1] {Saarbrücken qepHom''a'' 2015:src}, [2] {KLI mailing list 2020.03.30:src}'
    citations:
    - source: qephom_2015
      date: '2015'
    - source: kli_mailing_list
      date: '2020-03-30'
  translations:
    de:
      definition: Reihe (in einer Tabelle)
      notes: 'Außer der Reihe in einem Raster (wie in einer Tabellen oder anderer
        grafischer Darstellung) kann dies auch für materielle Dinge benutzt werden,
        wenn die Konfiguration einem Raster ähnelt (oder ähneln könnte) und es weitere
        Reihen gibt, nicht nur eine. Beispielsweise könnte man es für Reihen von Mais
        oder Reihen von Bäumen auf einem Feld oder Bauernhof benutzen. Man könnte
        es immer noch benutzen, wenn es nur eine Reihe gibt, in einer Situation in
        der es typischerweise mehrere gibt (oder es nicht überraschend wäre, wenn
        es mehrere gäbe). Wenn unklar ist, ob mehr als eine Reihe erwartet oder typisch
        ist, ist {wIyqap:n:nolink} wahrscheinlich die richtige Wahl.


        Das Wort {mIr:n:1} kann umgangssprachlich hierfür benutzt werden, wenn die
        Dinge klar sind.'
    fa:
      definition: ردیف (در یک جدول یا صفحه گسترده)
    sv:
      definition: rad (i en tabell eller ett kalkylblad)
    ru:
      definition: строка (в таблице или электронной таблице)
    zh_HK:
      definition: 行（在表格或電子表格中）
    pt:
      definition: linha (em uma tabela ou planilha de cálculo)
    fi:
      definition: rivi (taulukossa)
    fr:
      definition: ligne (dans un tableau ou une feuille de calcul)
      notes: 'Outre d''une ligne dans une grille (comme dans un tableau ou autre représentation
        graphique), ce mot peut s''utiliser pour des choses corporelles si la configuration
        global est (ou pourrait être) similaire à une grille et quand il y a (ou pourrait
        y avoir) autres lignes, pas seulement une. Par exemple, on l''utiliserait
        pour une rangée de maïs ou d''arbres plantés dans un champ ou sur une ferme.
        Il pourrait toujours être utilisé quand il n''y a qu''une seule ligne dans
        une situation où il y a typiquement plus (ou il ne serait pas surprenant s''il
        y avait plus). S''il n''est pas clair dans une situation si une ou plus de
        lignes sont expectées ou typiques, {wIyqap:n:nolink} est probablement le bon
        choix.


        Le mot {mIr:n:1} peut s''utiliser comme un terme familier pour ceci, si les
        choses sont claires.'

entries:

  slug: wIy_n_1
  part_of_speech: n:1

  section: main
  definition:
    text: schematic, graphic representation
    parts:
    - text: schematic
    - text: graphic representation
  see_also: '{pu''jIn:n}, {ren:v}'
  notes: This word might be translated as "schematic" or "graphic representation"
    or the like, and in military contexts it is used to refer to an abstract schematic
    of a battlefield. Used as ship's jargon, it refers to the "tactical display" mode
    of a {jIH:n:2,nolink} (see {wIy:n:2}).[1]
  sources:
    raw: '[1] {Saarbrücken qepHom''a'' 2023:src}'
    citations:
    - source: qephom_2023
      date: '2023'
  translations:
    de:
      definition: Schema, grafische Darstellung
      notes: Dieses Wort könnte als "Schema" oder "graphische Darstellung" oder so
        ähnlich übersetzt werden und wird in militärischen Zusammenhängen für ein
        abstraktes Schema eines Schlachtfelds benutzt. Im Raumfahrt-Jargon bezeichnet
        es den "taktische Anzeige"-Modus eines {jIH:n:2,nolink} (siehe {wIy:n:2}).[1]
    fa:
      definition: شماتیک، نمایش گرافیکی
    sv:
      definition: schematisk, grafisk framställning
    ru:
      definition: схематическое, графическое изображение
    zh_HK:
      definition: 示意圖、圖形表示
    pt:
      definition: representação esquemática e gráfica
    fi:
      definition: kaavio, graafinen esitys
    fr:
      definition: schéma, représentation graphique
      notes: Ce mot pourrait se traduire par "schéma" ou "représentation graphique"
        ou similaire et dans un contexte militaire s'utilise pour un schéma abstrait
        d'un champ de bataille. Dans le jargon astronautique, il se réfère au mode
        "affichage tactique" d'un {jIH:n:2,nolink} (voir {wIy:n:2}).[1]
- entry_name: wIy
  slug: wIy_n_2
  part_of_speech: n:2
  pos: n
  homophone: 2
  status: canonical
  section: main
  definition: tactical display (mode)
  see_also: '{cha'':v}, {HaSta:n:2}, {tlhat:n}'
  notes: 'This is actually the word for "schematic" (see {wIy:n:1}) which, when used
    as ship''s jargon, refers to the "tactical display" mode of a {jIH:n:2,nolink}.[4]


    Contrast this with {HaSta:n:2,nolink}, which is another display mode of a {jIH:n:2,nolink}.'
  hidden_notes: The first ever line of Klingon spoken on-screen was {wIy cha':sen@@wIy:n:2,
    cha':v}, in {Star Trek I:src}.
  examples: "\n▶ {wIy yIcha'!:sen}\n▶ {tlhIngan wIy:sen:nolink}\n   {'ejyo' luch rurbe'qu'\
    \ tlhIngan Duj luch. HoS law'qu' luch law'qu' je lo' Duj nuH pat Hub pat je. motlh\
    \ ray' luSamlaHmeH De' Qatlh cha' tlhIngan Duj jIH'a'. motlh pIm 'ejyo' Dujmey.:sen:nolink}\n\
    \  \"Klingon Tactical Display\n   Klingon starship design is vastly different\
    \ from Starfleet technology. A huge amount of the ship's power and technology\
    \ is devoted to its weapons grid and defensive systems. Anders als bei den meisten\
    \ Schiffen der Sternenflotte, ist der Hauptschirm eines klingonischen Schiffs\
    \ üblicherweise mit einem komplexen Zielerfassungsraster überlagert.\"[3]"
  sources:
    raw: '[1] {TKD:src}, [2] {Star Trek I:src}, [3] {SkyBox SP3:src} (reprinted in
      {HQ 3.4, p.10-11, Dec. 1994:src}), [4] {Saarbrücken qepHom''a'' 2023:src}'
    citations:
    - source: tkd
    - source: star_trek_i
    - source: skybox_sp3
      reprinted_in:
        source: holqed
        page_start: 10
        page_end: 11
        volume: 3
        issue: 4
        date: Dec. 1994
    - source: qephom_2023
      date: '2023'
  translations:
    de:
      definition: taktische Anzeige
      notes: 'Dies ist das Wort für "Schema" (siehe {wIy:n:1}), das im Raumfahrtjargon,
        den "taktische Anzeige"-Modus eines {jIH:n:2,nolink} bezeichnet.[4]


        Steht im Gegensatz zu {HaSta:n:2,nolink}, was ein anderer Anzeigemodus eines
        {jIH:n:2,nolink} ist.'
      examples: "\n▶ {wIy yIcha'!:sen}\n▶ {tlhIngan wIy:sen:nolink}\n   {'ejyo' luch\
        \ rurbe'qu' tlhIngan Duj luch. HoS law'qu' luch law'qu' je lo' Duj nuH pat\
        \ Hub pat je. motlh ray' luSamlaHmeH De' Qatlh cha' tlhIngan Duj jIH'a'. motlh\
        \ pIm 'ejyo' Dujmey.:sen:nolink}\n  \"Klingonische taktische Anzeige\n   Klingonisches\
        \ Raumschiffdesign unterscheidet sich stark von der Technologie der Sternenflotte.\
        \ Ein großer Anteil der Schiffsenergie und -technologie wird für seine Waffen-\
        \ und Verteidigungssysteme verwendet. Unlike most Starfleet vessels, the main\
        \ viewer on a Klingon ship is usually overlaid with a complex target acquisition\
        \ grid.\"[3]"
    fa:
      definition: نمایش تاکتیکی
    sv:
      definition: taktisk skärm (på monitor)
    ru:
      definition: тактическое отображение
    zh_HK:
      definition: 戰術展示
    pt:
      definition: display tático
    fi:
      definition: taktinen näkymä (avaruusaluksen näytöllä)
      notes: Aluksen näytöllä ({jIH:n:2}) voi näkyä valokuvaa aluksen ulkopuolelta
        ({HaSta:n:2,nolink}) tai taktinen kaavio taistelukentästä ({wIy:n:1,nolink}).
    fr:
      definition: affichage tactique (mode)
      notes: 'C''est en vérité le mot pour "schéma" (voir {wIy:n:1}) qui, dans le
        jargon astronautique, se réfère au mode "affichage tactique" d''un {jIH:n:2,nolink}.[4]


        À contraster avec {HaSta:n:2,nolink}, qui est un autre mot d''affichage d''un
        {jIH:n:2,nolink}.'
      examples: "\n▶ {wIy yIcha'!:sen}\n▶ {tlhIngan wIy:sen:nolink}\n   {'ejyo' luch\
        \ rurbe'qu' tlhIngan Duj luch. HoS law'qu' luch law'qu' je lo' Duj nuH pat\
        \ Hub pat je. motlh ray' luSamlaHmeH De' Qatlh cha' tlhIngan Duj jIH'a'. motlh\
        \ pIm 'ejyo' Dujmey.:sen:nolink}\n  \"Affichage tactique klingonne\n   Le\
        \ design des vaisseaux spatiaux klingons est très différent de la technologie\
        \ de Starfleet. Une grande partie de l'énérgie et de la technologie d'un vaisseau\
        \ est dévoué au réseau d'armement et systèmes défensives. Contrairement à\
        \ la plupart des vaisseaux de Starfleet, la visionneuse principale est généralement\
        \ recouvert d'une grille d'acquisition de la cible compliquée.\"[3]"

entry:
  entry_name: wIyqap
  slug: wIyqap_n
  part_of_speech: n
  pos: n
  status: canonical
  section: main
  definition: row or line (of people or things not expected to be in motion)
  see_also: '{lanSoy:n}, {wev:n}'
  notes: This might be used for a police lineup. The constituents of a {wIyqap:n:nolink}
    are not expected to move (in contrast to those in a {lanSoy:n:nolink}). This word
    is used even if the people or things are bunched up. It's also used if there is
    more than one line, when typically there's only one, so that in a police lineup
    with two rows, each is still a {wIyqap:n:nolink} (and not a {wev:n:nolink}).[1]
  examples: '

    ▶ {Ho'' wIyqap:n@@Ho'':n:1, wIyqap:n}'
  search_tags: lineup, line-up
  sources:
    raw: '[1] {KLI mailing list 2020.04.21:src}'
    citations:
    - source: kli_mailing_list
      date: '2020-04-21'
  translations:
    de:
      definition: Reihe (von stillstehenden Personen oder Gegenständen)
      notes: Dies könnte für eine Gegenüberstellung (mit den Verdächtigen in einer
        Reihe) verwendet werden. Man erwartet nicht, dass sich die Teile einer {wIyqap:n:nolink}
        bewegen (im Gegensatz zu denen einer {lanSoy:n:nolink}). Dieses Wort wird
        benutzt auch wenn die Personen oder Gegenstände zusammengedückt sind. Es wird
        auch benutzt, wenn es mehr als eine Reihe gibt, solange es normalerweise nur
        eine gibt. Wenn eines Gegenüberstellung zwei Reihen hat, ist jede immernoch
        eine {wIyqap:n:nolink} (und keine {wev:n:nolink}).[1]
    fa:
      definition: ردیف یا خط (از افراد یا چیزهایی که انتظار نمی رود در حرکت باشد)

      definition: rad eller rad (av människor eller saker som inte förväntas vara
        i rörelse)
    ru:
      definition: строка или строка (людей или предметов, которые не должны находиться
        в движении)
    zh_HK:
      definition: 一行或一行（預期不會運動的人或事物）
    pt:
      definition: fila ou linha (de pessoas ou coisas que não se espera que estejam
        em movimento)
    fi:
      definition: rivi tai jono (paikallaan olevia asioita tai ihmisiä)
    fr:
      definition: rangée, rang ou ligne (de personnes ou de choses qu'on ne s'attend
        pas être en mouvement)

        les suspects dans une rangée). Les constituants d'une {wIyqap:n:nolink} ne
        sont pas censé bouger (au contraire de ceux dans une {lanSoy:n:nolink}). Ce
        mot s'utilise même quand les personnes ou les choses sont serrés. Il s'utilise
        aussi quand il y a plus d'une rangée quand il n'y a typiquement qu'une seule.
        Si une séance d'identification a deux rangées de suspects, chacune est toujours
        une {wIyqap:n:nolink} (et pas une {wev:n:nolink}).[1]

entries:
- entry_name: yaD
  slug: yaD_n_1
  part_of_speech: n:1,body
  pos: n
  pos_subtype: body
  homophone: 1
  status: canonical
  section: main
  definition: toe
  see_also: '{qam:n}, {nItlh:n}'
  notes: 'Klingon has five verbs corresponding to each of the {yaD:n:1,nolink}: {mar:v},
    {Hom:v}, {roS:v:2}, {nan:v:2}, and {Qay'':v:2}.


    Correspondingly, the five toes are {marwI'':n}, {HomwI'':n}, {roSwI'':n}, {nanwI'':n:2},
    and {Qay''wI'':n}.


    The toe verbs are used in the same way as the finger verbs, but they are not heard
    often outside of discussions about martial arts movements or dance, and are normally
    considered archaic.'
  hidden_notes: The verbs for the toes come from the nursery rhyme "This Little Piggy".
  sources:
    raw: '[1] {TKD:src}, [2] {HQ 10.2, Jun. 2001:src}'
    citations:
    - source: tkd
    - source: holqed
      volume: 10
      issue: 2
      date: Jun. 2001
  translations:
    de:
      definition: Zehe
      notes: "Klingonisch hat fünf Verben, die jedem der fünf {yaD:n:1,nolink} entsprechen:\
        \ {mar:v}, {Hom:v}, {roS:v:2}, {nan:v:2}, und {Qay':v:2}.\n\n        Dementsprechend\
        \ sind die fünf Zehen {marwI':n}, {HomwI':n}, {roSwI':n}, {nanwI':n:2}, und\
        \ {Qay'wI':n}.\n\n        Die Zehen-Verben werden auf die gleiche Art benutzt\
        \ wie die Finger-Verben, aber sie werden nicht oft außerhalb von Gesprächen\
        \ über Kampfsportbewegungen oder Tanz und gelten normalerweise als archaisch."
    fa:
      definition: انگشت پا
    sv:
      definition: tå
    ru:
      definition: палец на ноге
    zh_HK:
      definition: 腳趾
    pt:
      definition: dedo do pé
    fi:
      definition: varvas
    fr:
      definition: orteil, doigt de pied
      notes: "Le klingon a cinq verbes qui correspondent à chacun des {yaD:n:1,nolink}:\
        \ {mar:v}, {Hom:v}, {roS:v:2}, {nan:v:2}, et {Qay':v:2}.\n\n        Les cinq\
        \ orteils sont donc {marwI':n}, {HomwI':n}, {roSwI':n}, {nanwI':n:2}, et {Qay'wI':n}.\n\
        \n        Les verbes des orteils sont utilisés de la même manière que les\
        \ verbes des doigts, mais ne s'utilisent pas souvent en dehors de conversations\
        \ sur les mouvement d'art martial ou la dance et sont normalement considérés\
        \ archaïques."

entry:
  entry_name: yaH
  slug: yaH_n
  part_of_speech: n:klcp1
